compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
`.github/llm-providers/openai.toml` (the provider overlay that the `external LLM (live openai)` arm of the `Live External Integration` workflow selects through `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE`) sets `[llm.model_classes] trivial = { model = "openai-responses:gpt-5.4-nano" }`. OpenAI's model catalogue (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/all, read 2026-11-10 PST) lists `gpt-5.4-nano` under "Deprecated models" with status "Deprecated" and names no successor. `gpt-5.4-mini` (standard slot) and `gpt-5.5` (frontier/scalar slot, moved by deceptive-banal-baboon, Gerrit 3336) carry no deprecation badge.

When OpenAI retires the model, every trivial-class call on the openai arm will fail and turn the workflow red again for a reason unrelated to rebar code.

Found while working deceptive-banal-baboon; not worked (hold on new bugs).

## Open questions for the plan
- Which current OpenAI model replaces the trivial slot. The catalogue names no replacement for nano; candidates must be checked against the pinned `pydantic-ai-slim` 1.x model profiles (GPT-6 models need the 2.x major upgrade, per docs/ci-provider-matrix.md).
- Whether OpenAI has published a retirement date (the "Deprecated models" page).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The openai overlay's trivial slot names a model the OpenAI catalogue does not mark deprecated, with the choice and source recorded in docs/ci-provider-matrix.md and .github/llm-providers/README.md.
- [ ] tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py still passes for the overlay.
- [ ] [non-codebase] A `Live External Integration` run on main after the change shows `external LLM (live openai)` concluding success; run id recorded on this ticket.
